ranking.why: The patient's mitoses per ten high-power fields of 20 and strong immunoreactivity for CD31, CD99, and Fli-1 support this diagnosis based on the reference material for Solitary Fibrous Tumor/Hemangiopericytoma.

The patient's strong immunoreactivity for CD31, CD99, and Fli-1 and the presence of a left tentorial extra-axial enhancing mass support this diagnosis based on the reference material for Solitary Fibrous Tumor.

The patient's strong immunoreactivity for CD31, CD99, and Fli-1 and the presence of a left tentorial extra-axial enhancing mass support this diagnosis based on the reference material for Hemangiopericytoma.
The reference material for Hemangioma does not provide sufficient information to support or rule out this diagnosis based on the patient's symptoms and test results.

The patient's mitoses per ten high-power fields of 20 contradicts the typical feature of Meningioma, which has mitotic figures of <= 20 per 10 high-power fields (HPF), as stated in the reference material.
The patient's lack of lymph nodes involvement and absence of B-symptoms contradict the typical features of Lymphoma, as stated in the reference material.
The patient's lack of distant metastasis and absence of multiple primary tumors contradict the typical features of Metastasis, as stated in the reference material.
The reference material for Cavernous angioma does not provide sufficient information to support or rule out this diagnosis based on the patient's symptoms and test results.

The patient's lack of immunosuppression, human herpesvirus/Kaposi sarcoma herpesvirus (HHV-8) infection, and absence of violaceous pink to purple plaques contradict the typical features of Kaposi's sarcoma, as stated in the reference material.
